subject: computer-science
title: OOP: Classes, Objects and Encapsulation
welcome_lead: Bundle state and behaviour — and hide what should be hidden.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: classes, objects, fields, methods and encapsulation.
final_note: Encapsulation is the first pillar of OOP.

concepts.def: A blueprint defining fields and methods for objects.
An instance of a class with its own field values.
Hiding internal state behind a public interface.
A data member of an object — its state.
A function defined inside a class.
A special method called when an object is created.

walkthroughs.body_html: A class is a template (Dog). An object is a concrete instance (myDog = Dog('Rex')). One class produces many independent objects with their own state.
Mark fields as private and expose them only through methods (getters/setters). This stops external code breaking invariants and lets you change internals later without changing the interface.
A constructor runs when new creates an object. It initialises fields so the object starts in a valid state. Many languages allow overloaded constructors with different parameter lists.
